answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day renewal deadline create severe pressure, but the 94% volume utilization leaves no safety margin for supply disruption. Switching vendors (memory_c2) delivered cost wins but risks onboarding friction during a capacity-constrained period. Deferring (memory_c5) is not viable given the hard expiry and mandate. Renewing (memory_c1) without negotiation wastes the leverage created by the deadline and mandate. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is valuable for risk but doesn't meet the 18% cost target alone. Renegotiating with the incumbent (memory_c4) has demonstrated success at prior renewal and can combine the multi-year volume pricing precedent (memory_c6) with the incumbent's cost performance (memory_c2 shows market is aggressive) to hit the margin target while preserving supply continuity. Verification of memory_c4 will confirm the magnitude of prior renegotiation gains and negotiation approach. The high line utilization and two-week timeline make negotiated renewal with incumbent the lowest-risk path to the 18% target. This is not yet a second-source decision, but flagged as downstream value risk if renegotiation yields insufficient margin—at that point multi-vendor strategy becomes necessary.
